English | 中文 | Español | Português | हिन्दी
Expose the running DeepSeek Harness Web GUI's **authenticated URL** as an agent tool, so browser aut
omation and scripts can open the GUI instead of hitting `401 dsh web authentication required`.
It also ships **temporary authenticated DSH Web**: an agent (`dsh_web_start` / `dsh_web_restart` / `
dsh_web_stop` / `dsh_web_status` tools) or a person (`/dsh-web` command — start when absent, restart
in place when running) can get a per-session instance with its own throwaway `DSH_HOME` and port, t
o exercise new plugins, surfaces, or profiles without touching the live session — one per session, s
essions never disturb each other, and an instance only ever exists as a tracked background job bound
disturb each other, and an instance only ever exists as a tracked background job bound to a session.
## The problem
`dsh --profile web` mints a random launch token per process and prints it once:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`GET /?token=...` verifies the token, sets a signed cookie bound to host:port, and redirects to `/`.
Opening the bare address returns:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The Desktop edition starts its own Host process on a random port and never prints that line, so any
external browser or automation tool opening `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` always gets 401. There is no
`--no-browser-auth` switch today.
## How it works
The plugin runs inside the Host process and asks the official public API `connection.authenticatedUr
l(baseUrl)` — the same call `dsh web` uses to build the URL it prints — then returns the result as a
the same call `dsh web` uses to build the URL it prints — then returns the result as a tool result.
It never reads the cookie-signing secret in `$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml` and never mints a cookie i
tself, so the URL is a genuine first-party session bound to this process.
Base URL resolution prefers `webApp.getAdvertisedUrl()` (respects `--public-url` and mounts), then `
webServer.getOrigin()`, then protocol plus loopback port. Every call re-reads the live value, so ran
dom Desktop ports and restarted tokens need no cache. The token is attached only when that base is a
bsolute `http` or `https`, has no username or password, and — unless the plugin config sets `allowPu
blic: true` — names a loopback host (`127.0.0.0/8`, `localhost`, or `::1`). The returned URL must be
that same origin and carry exactly one `token`. An unacceptable base is refused before `authenticat
edUrl` is called, and the error text never includes the URL.

## Security
- The returned URL contains **this process's launch token**. It is a credential equivalent to a sign

ed-in session and only works while the Host process is alive.
- Do not write it to logs, commit it,

or paste it into chats. Regenerate by calling the tool again; a restart invalidates it.
- A successf
ul call still places the token in the session transcript and in later model requests. "Do not write
it to logs" does not stop the host from storing the tool result. That is a wider audience than the o

ne line `dsh web` prints in a terminal.
- The plugin does not read `.credentials.yaml` and does not

mint cookies.
- Non-loopback URLs (`--public-url`, a LAN address, or `0.0.0.0`) are refused unless t

he plugin config is exactly `allowPublic: true`. That flag trusts the advertised host.
- An isolated
instance is a real `dsh web` child process. With `shareApiKey: true` (the default) it receives this
process's `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` through its environment: not written to the temporary home and not pri
nted, but readable by any process running as the same user, and every turn inside it bills the same

account. `shareApiKey: false` opts out.
- `install` runs pnpm's lifecycle scripts for the named pack
ages as your user. Specs are character-checked (no spaces, quotes, or `&|<>^`), which blocks shell i
njection into the install command but says nothing about a well-formed malicious package. `allowInst

all: false` rejects install requests outright.
- The exposure arguments (`host`, `public_url`, `tls_
cert`/`tls_key`, `trusted_host`) are accepted only behind `allowPublic: true`, and `host` refuses wi
ldcards even then. Once it is on, the reachable network is the token's audience; TLS does not shrink

that audience.
- Stopping ends the process tree (`taskkill /T` on Windows) and deletes the temporar
y home. The startup sweep only kills a leftover process when its recorded port still answers with DS

H's 401 signature, so a reused PID is never killed by mistake.
- It is unrelated to Discussion #8678
(reading the signing secret inside a sandbox to forge cookies): this plugin never touches that secr
eading the signing secret inside a sandbox to forge cookies): this plugin never touches that secret.
## Compatibility
| Item | Value |

`0.2.1-rc.2` and `0.2.2-rc.1`, Windows x64, desktop and web profiles |
| Web combination | needs th
e `connection` service; a profile without a Web GUI reports a clear error |
Display metadata (`locale/*.json` plus the exported `./icon`) makes the Plugins page and Settings sh
ow a proper title, description and artwork instead of the raw package id. The plugin does not requir
e a build step: it ships plain ESM JavaScript.
